prompt:

Image 1 is the sole character/art source. Image 2 is an enlarged LOCAL POSITIONING GUIDE to the same area of image 1; it is not another scene or cel.

Make the very small motion marked in image 2: translate the SAME hand and SAME watermelon only 38 original pixels to screen-right and 28 original pixels down, keeping their exact original size and angle. Follow the CYAN single hand-and-fruit outline as the destination. The green contour preserves the original red flesh and its concave bite notch. Replace the faded OLD hand/fruit completely, never keep both positions. Adjust just the connected bent forearm and sleeve opening to reach the purple wrist/elbow positions naturally. There must remain exactly two arms and two hands in the whole character. Do not place the fruit near the center of her chest or move it farther right than the cyan outline.

Guide coordinates are in original full-frame pixels: the guide covers x350–720/y420–800 and is displayed at 2x for readability. Target red flesh bounding box x466–561/y501–602; target wrist around (518,661), elbow (516,749). The entire fruit should end near x569 on its right edge, well left of x607. This is a tiny right/down shift, not a large swing. Keep the fruit's three black seeds in the exact same arrangement, same curved green rind, same already missing bite at the upper-right tip. The bite is genuinely missing flesh with the background/body behind visible, never a white patch.

Preserve every other part of image 1 as closely as possible: the head, hair, clip, glasses, facial expression, pupils/gaze, mouth, torso, blouse flower pattern, buttons, stationary screen-right arm and bangle, basin, pods and dish. Preserve the illustrated linework, flat neutral lighting, colors, full composition and original 1670x942 canvas. No text, arrows, contours, guide marks, background or shadows from image 2 in the output. Keep genuinely transparent alpha outside the original cutout character and objects. Return one full-resolution finished cel.
